                                       JOHN M. BURROW’S

                   ADDENDUM TO APPEAL OF SOAH ORDER NO. 25

         TO THE HONORABLE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS

       John M. Burrow ("Mr. Burrow, me, my, I, mine, etc.”), a pro se intervenor, timely files

this addendum to his appeal of State Office of Administrative Hearings (“SOAH”) Order No. 25

(59475-5331): Denying Mr. Burrow’s Motion for Relief for Failure to Provide Required Notice.

       Mr. Burrow respectfully shows as follows:



                                 I.     EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
       Mr. Burrow brought his appeal because SOAH Order No. 25 denies owners of over 1,300

directly affected properties, including Mr. Burrow’s property, the relief due them in accordance

with 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5), due to Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC’s

(“Oncor’s”) and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation’s (“LCRA TSC’s”)(collectively,

“Applicants’”) failure to comply with 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(4). SOAH Order No. 25


BURROW 59475 – Addendum to Appeal to SOAH Order No. 25                                  Page 1 of 5
 also denies relief due David and Amy Hillock, the relief due them in accordance with 16 Tex.

Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5), due to Applicants’ failure to obtain current county tax rolls, as

required by 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(3).

       New information has come to light in the Applicants’ recent responses to RFIs from

directly affected landowner intervenors, which also questioned the Applicants’ compliance with

16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(3) based on the Applicants’ apparent failure to obtain current

county tax rolls, as required by 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(3).



                 II.   APPLICANTS DIVULGED THEY DID NOT OBTAIN
                                 CURRENT COUNTY TAX ROLLS

A. On Wednesday, June 3, 2026, at 07:58:54 PM, Applicants posted their “RESPONSE TO

   ANNA THORNTON’S FIRST REQUEST FOR INFORMATION” (59475-5768). This was

   posted after the SOAH “ordered” deadline to submit exhibits into evidence for the Hearing

   on Merits. This morning Kevin Kennedy, a pro se landowner intervenor, has added 59475-

   5768 to his exhibits for hearing evidence, but since it is past the deadline, we expect there

   will be significant efforts to keep the damning information contained in the Applicants’ RFI

   response from being entered into the record.

B. In the Applicants’ response to Ms. Thorton’s RFI, they divulge that they used 2025 address

   data for mailing of landowner notification of 59475 application, on March 26, 2026, failing

   to comply with 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(3). (See Attachment 1, at p. 17)

C. In the Applicants’ response to Ms. Thorton’s RFI, they divulge that they have already

   identified twenty-seven (27) current landowners who were not notified because Applicants

   did not obtain current county tax rolls, as required by 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(3).

   (See Attachment 1, at p. 28). This is exactly what I stated occurred in the motion for remedy

   and relief (59475-5123) and in the appeal of SOAH Order No. 25 (59475-5331).

BURROW 59475 – Addendum to Appeal to SOAH Order No. 25                                    Page 2 of 5
 D. On Wednesday, June 3, 2026, at 03:02:40 PM, Applicants posted a “SUPPLEMENTAL

   AFFIDAVIT ATTESTING TO THE PROVISION OF NOTICE” (59475-5595). This

   document identifies the Applicants’ most recent notification mailings as June 1, 2026, which

   is sixty-seven (67) days after March 26, 2026, when these landowners were required to be

   notified.

E. These landowners are owed a sixty-seven (67) day extension in all elements of the 59475 and

   59182 procedurals schedules, in accordance with 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5).

F. The twenty-seven (27) non-notified landowners, listed in the Applicants’ response to Ms.

   Thorton’s RFI, appear to be only those who acquired newly subdivided property. It does not

   include landowners who simply acquired property after the Applicants obtained the 2025

   ownership data, but before March 26, 2026, such as David and Amy Hillock, who we

   describe in our original motion and appeal. There are more non-notified landowners yet to be

   identified and more remedy and relief that is lawfully owed.

G. The Commission must act swiftly and decisively on this matter. There has been a tremendous

   breach of trust and violation of the public interest. The Applicants, whether attempting to

   game the system or whether through incompetence, have denied dozens of landowners their

   right of due process. Thus far, SOAH appears to be a willing participant in this egregious act

   of landowner abuse, seemingly crippled by their unwavering allegiance to an arbitrary and

   capricious 180-day deadline.




BURROW 59475 – Addendum to Appeal to SOAH Order No. 25                                   Page 3 of 5
                                             III. PRAYER

       Landowners across Texas are wondering what it will take for their rights to be recognized

and protected. They are wondering who in our State agencies and government will come to their

aid and defense. There will be tremendous scrutiny regarding how the Commission exercises its

agency discretion in this matter. If these actions by the Applicants and SOAH are not sufficient

to trigger 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5), then what will? If 16 Tex. Admin. Code

22.52.(a).(5) is not applied here, now, then why is it even in the Code?



       Mr. Burrow appeals SOAH Order No. 25 and respectfully requests that the Commission:

       -   POSTPONE the Hearing on Merit so all affected landowners have the lawful allotted

           time and right to participate.

       -   OVERRULE SOAH Order No. 25 and GRANT the full remedy and relief requested

           in my motion, in accordance with 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5).

       -   COMPEL the Applicant to immediately obtain proper current county tax rolls and

           notify all affected landowners not notified in their original March 26, 2026,

           notification of application. The number of total non-notified landowners is unknown

           at this time, and this ongoing lack of due process must be remedied.

       -   COMPEL the SOAH Administrative Law Judges to GRANT proper and full relief to

           any newly identified affected property owners, including the over 1,300 not allowed

           to participate in the public meeting process, who were not previously notified of the

           application, in accordance with 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5).

       -   Considering new evidence revealed by the Applicants after the June 3, 2026 07:00PM

           evidentiary exhibit deadline, COMPEL the SOAH Administration Law Judges to

           allow inclusion of ANY documents related to landowner notifications for public

           meetings and the application prior to be included in the Hearing on Merit evidentiary

           record, whether they be known or yet to be discovered, and whether they be dated


BURROW 59475 – Addendum to Appeal to SOAH Order No. 25                                     Page 4 of 5
            before or after the March 26, 2026 application submission, without restriction to

           previously established procedural schedules.

       -   COMPEL the applicants to respond Mr. Kennedy's RFI 17 requesting the dates

           applicants pulled each county' s tax rolls with property ownership data for the mailing

           addresses used for both the June 2025 public meeting notices and the March 26, 2026

           application notices.

       -   GRANT other and further relief to which the parties may be entitled

       -   RESTORE the People’s faith in their State government.



Date Signed: June 4, 2026
